scientific_question: Does the transported P_T/a_T functional asymmetry remain valid when the same 32 Liu support presentations are temporally rearranged, or does it depend on the original blockwise-random presentation regime?
current_theory: P_T implements state-dependent iterative global reassembly and may express quantitative order sensitivity, whereas a_T is an exactly additive edge ledger whose terminal state is algebraically presentation-order invariant. The functional division should survive temporal rearrangement even if the final P_T field is not numerically invariant.
primary_hypothesis: On the source-correct original Liu graph, blockwise-random, relation-clustered, and exact reverse schedules made from the same subject-specific trial multiset will all retain competent constructive rankings and the same P_T/a_T double dissociation. The a_T ledger and Gram read will additionally be exactly invariant to the three orderings in common float64 arithmetic.
claim_boundary: A pass supports development transport across these three registered presentation regimes on the original eight-item Liu graph and three frozen backbones. It does not establish arbitrary temporal robustness, spacing or recency invariance, network-population prevalence, graph-by-order interaction, a human or biological mechanism, or invariance of the high-dimensional P_T state or its exact output field.

fixed_task_contract.same_subject_trial_multiset: For each virtual participant, all schedules contain exactly the same 32 SupportTrial values: item pair, higher/lower identity, signed magnitude, and left-right orientation. Only temporal position and its derived block index change.
fixed_task_contract.fixed_model: Reuse the same checkpoints, local gains, v2.4 differential evidence admission, P_T update, a_T address/write/read, tanh, W_out, temperature, cue codes, subject encoding states, and query schedules.
fixed_task_contract.only_manipulation: permutation of the 32 already generated passive support presentations

schedule_contract.blockwise_random: The unchanged RankingProtocol.support_schedule generated with support_seed 31101 plus subject index: four temporal blocks, every support relation once per block, independently randomized within block.
schedule_contract.relation_clustered: Stable-sort each subject's unchanged blockwise-random trial list by the relation's index in protocol.support_pairs_higher_lower. Preserve the original relative order of that relation's four presentations. The result has four consecutive presentations per relation in the protocol's fixed relation order.
schedule_contract.reverse: Reverse each subject's complete unchanged 32-trial blockwise-random list exactly.
schedule_contract.block_index_reassignment: After either nonbaseline permutation, assign block_index=floor(new_trial_index/8). Block index is metadata; the model receives the unchanged registered trial-index time grid.
schedule_contract.gain_reassembly: Because stable omission is relation-specific, rebuild subject_trial_gains from the frozen subject_relation_gains and each transformed trial's relation. No admission value is resampled.
schedule_contract.integrity: For every subject and variant, the trial multiset excluding block_index must be byte-identical to baseline, each relation must occur four times, relation-specific admission must match baseline, and all transformed schedule hashes must be fixed in the result.

evaluation.bootstrap_seed_rule: 760000 + 100 * backbone_seed + schedule_index, with schedule_index one through three in registered order
evaluation.bootstrap_unit: virtual participant within one schedule and one backbone
evaluation.execution: One bounded GPU process through a prospectively source-locked wrapper that calls fsrl.formal_runtime.configure_formal_runtime before importing the evaluator; evaluate schedule order as registered and seed order 2101, 2102, 2103.

conditions_and_estimands.within_schedule_estimands: Reuse the exact topology-v1 definitions for exact decision competence, correct probability, Hodge additivity, transitive coherence, Hodge-to-true tau, sampled ranking individualization/stability, global remote and third-party relation-LOO, a-off learned probability loss, P-off local scope, and exact a_T ledger/Gram reconstruction.
conditions_and_estimands.cross_schedule_local_identity: In common float64 arithmetic compare each nonbaseline terminal a_T ledger state and all 28 Gram reads with blockwise_random for the same participant. Maximum absolute errors must be at most 1e-12.
conditions_and_estimands.cross_schedule_global_diagnostics: For a-off P_T fields, report participant-level Pearson correlation, centered RMSE, exact decision agreement, Hodge-potential Kendall tau, and changes in remote LOO magnitude for each nonbaseline schedule versus blockwise_random. These are descriptive and cannot rescue or veto the registered functional gates.
conditions_and_estimands.secondary_behavior: Report sampled learned/nonlearned/overall accuracy, symbolic-distance slope, serial-position endpoint, ranking classes, stable errors, and inter-subject ranking diversity for every cell without human calibration.

primary_links.intact_competence: Within every schedule-backbone cell, participant-bootstrap lower bounds for intact learned and nonlearned exact decision accuracy both exceed 0.50.
primary_links.constructive_global_structure: Within every cell, intact and a-off Hodge-fraction lower bounds are at least 0.95, intact transitive-triplet lower bound is at least 0.95, and intact Hodge-order tau-to-true lower bound exceeds zero.
primary_links.individualized_stable_structure: Within every cell, at least two eligible non-correct subjects exist, inter-subject tau upper bound is below 0.80, and 80-percent stable-error prevalence lower bound is at least 0.80.
primary_links.P_off_global_collapse: Within every cell, P-off/a-on nonlearned correct-probability upper bound is at most 0.55 and P-off local remote minus 0.25 times intact global remote upper bound is below zero.
primary_links.P_remote_reassembly: Within every cell, global a-off disjoint relation-LOO and third-party relational lower bounds both exceed zero.
primary_links.a_off_direct_loss: Within every cell, intact minus a-off learned correct-probability lower bound exceeds zero.
primary_links.P_off_a_on_direct_nontransitive: Within every cell, P-off/a-on learned correct-probability lower bound exceeds 0.50 and learned-minus-nonlearned lower bound exceeds zero.
primary_links.exact_order_invariant_local_algorithm: Every within-schedule algebraic tensor/read error is at most 1e-6 and every nonbaseline-versus-baseline float64 terminal ledger/read error is at most 1e-12.

outcome_tree.cell: A schedule-backbone cell passes only if all eight links and all source, artifact, schedule-multiset, gain-reassembly, GPU-runtime, tensor-freeze, orientation, finite-value, and exactness integrity gates pass.
outcome_tree.schedule: A schedule transports only if it passes independently in all three backbones.
outcome_tree.LIU_PRESENTATION_ORDER_MECHANISM_TRANSPO: All three schedules transport. Promote the asymmetric computation as development-supported across the tested Liu graph and presentation regimes, while retaining quantitative order effects and the claim boundary.
outcome_tree.ORDER_DEPENDENT_OR_UNRESOLVED: One or two schedules transport or a primary link is heterogeneous across competent backbones. Localize only the registered global field diagnostics before any new schedule family; do not add order conditions post hoc.
outcome_tree.FUNCTIONAL_ASYMMETRY_NOT_ORDER_TRANSPORT: All schedule-backbone cells are competent and interpretable but neither nonbaseline schedule transports the complete division. Retain topology transport under blockwise random presentation and reject presentation-order transport.
outcome_tree.PRESENTATION_ORDER_COMPETENCE_NOT_ESTABL: Any schedule-backbone cell fails intact competence. Its mechanism result is non-interpretable; do not tune the order, graph, model, gain, temperature, or threshold.
outcome_tree.NONINTERPRETABLE_EXECUTION: Any integrity gate fails. Repair execution under a separately recorded lock without changing schedule transforms, science, or thresholds.

stop_rules: Do not change schedules, schedule order, graph, seeds, participant count, trial multiset, admission, gains, temperature, bootstrap, thresholds, estimands, or outcome tree after implementation or evaluation.
Do not require exact P_T state or field invariance; P_T is registered as state-dependent and interacting. Functional gates, not output equality, decide transport.
Do not tune symbolic-distance slope, serial-position endpoints, or original seed inconsistency on any schedule.
Do not begin sparsity, item-count, list-linking, classic transitive-inference, Miconi-ancestry, MEG, or human-mechanism work before this result is frozen. If transported, sparsity is next.
